section_summary: This section concerns efforts to resume imports of Japanese seed oysters for Pacific Coast growers and sets out U.S. occupation policy for Japanese fisheries. It also contains correspondence about cultured pearls and records of an investigation into Joseph Goldstone and Howard MacGowan’s pearl purchases while travelling on an official mission. The last letter, concerning pearls seized from Goldstone, continues beyond page 77.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning importation of Japanese seed oysters
subfiles.about: The Interior Department asks State to help Pacific Coast growers resume seed-oyster imports from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The letter explains the industry’s dependence on Japanese seed oysters, encloses growers’ correspondence, and recommends export arrangements that avoid the former single-exporter monopoly.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing appeal to General MacArthur
subfiles.about: Mathias seeks help obtaining Japanese seed oysters and objects to Yamishita’s renewed trade efforts.
subfiles.summary: Mathias reports poor recent oyster sets in Washington waters and encloses the association’s appeal to MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Request for information on seed oysters from Sendai Bay
subfiles.about: The oyster growers ask when and how they can resume direct purchases from Sendai Bay producers.
subfiles.summary: Mathias recounts the prewar trade, the association’s efforts to protect growers, and its preference for inspected Sendai Bay seed. He asks about the 1945 catch, available quantities, contacts, and the reopening of trade.

subfiles.title: Reply on proposed seed-oyster imports
subfiles.about: State says it has asked the Supreme Commander about seed oysters for the coming growing season.
subfiles.summary: The reply promises to consider growers’ needs when choosing exports under occupation trade directives.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of fishing and aquatic industries policy
subfiles.about: The coordinating committee transmits its approved policy paper on Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Matthews forwards SWNCC 99/3 for guidance and implementation.

subfiles.title: Policy with Respect to Fishing and Aquatic Industries in Japan
subfiles.to: State, War and Navy Departments; Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: The paper sets occupation policy for Japanese fisheries, aquatic industries, exports, and conservation.
subfiles.summary: The policy prioritizes coastal fisheries and fish culture for Japan’s food needs, while allowing wider fishing only when necessary and consistent with security and international rights. It calls for rehabilitating vessels and processing facilities, collecting resource data, observing conservation and whaling rules, and restricting fishing near Allied territories. Its appendices explain prewar production, wartime decline, food needs, Soviet fishing rights, and sealing concerns.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: A filing slip records a charged enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip for an enclosure.

subfiles.title: Reply to Eldon Griffin on oyster imports, incomplete copy
subfiles.about: State explains that occupation controls prevent direct private trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: First-page copy of a reply continued in the following duplicate.

subfiles.title: Reply to Eldon Griffin on oyster imports
subfiles.about: State says it is investigating seed-oyster availability while maintaining Allied control of Japanese trade.
subfiles.summary: The reply says direct private trade cannot yet resume and assures Griffin that export prospects are being examined.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Senate committee travellers
subfiles.about: Woodard recommends referring a sensitive telegram about Senate committee travellers to Kermit Gordon.
subfiles.summary: He identifies Gordon as the officer familiar with the trip arrangements.

subfiles.title: Reply to Eldon Griffin on expected seed-oyster exports
subfiles.about: State reports that Japanese seed oysters may become exportable from December 1946.
subfiles.summary: Martin estimates 10,000 cases through March 1947 and directs growers to the U.S. Commercial Company.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note from Eldon Griffin
subfiles.about: A largely illegible handwritten note is filed with Griffin’s correspondence.
subfiles.summary: The note’s substance is not legible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram on pearls and seed oysters
subfiles.about: The consulate reports inquiries by Goldstone and MacGowan about pearls and seed oysters.
subfiles.summary: An incomplete, noisy telegram copy reports a continuing CID inquiry.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Shanghai telegram 378
subfiles.about: Goldstone’s cultured-pearl inquiries and MacGowan’s seed-oyster interest are reported.
subfiles.summary: CID had found contacts but no confirmed transaction.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Shanghai telegram 378
subfiles.about: A second copy reports Goldstone’s pearl inquiries and MacGowan’s interest in seed oysters.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate paraphrase of telegram 378.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Shanghai on CID inquiry
subfiles.about: State limits what the consulate may disclose to CID about the two travellers.
subfiles.summary: State permits informal cooperation but reserves Senator Murray’s correspondence and discourages formal staff statements.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram 388 on detention and seized pearls
subfiles.about: The consulate reports Goldstone’s removal from an aircraft and seeks instructions on CID access.
subfiles.summary: Army investigators seized pearls Goldstone intended to carry by military air transport and planned to send him and MacGowan home by ship. The consul asks whether staff, invoices, and cables may be examined.

subfiles.title: War Department cable urging action against MacGowan
subfiles.to: War Department; Smaller War Plants Corporation
subfiles.about: Maverick condemns alleged private pearl trading during an official trip.
subfiles.summary: He urges termination of MacGowan’s employment and related support, notification of the Senate committee, and cooperation with investigators.

subfiles.title: Brief paraphrase of Shanghai telegram 378
subfiles.about: A summary links Goldstone to cultured pearls and MacGowan to Japanese seed oysters.
subfiles.summary: The summary notes that the CID investigation was continuing.

subfiles.title: Return of Goldstone–MacGowan case file
subfiles.about: Blake returns a case file because his division’s work is complete.
subfiles.summary: He asks Summers to arrange proper filing.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note
subfiles.about: A cable is returned for possible use in later developments.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten file-routing note.

subfiles.title: Second paraphrase of Maverick’s War Department cable
subfiles.to: War Department; Smaller War Plants Corporation
subfiles.about: A second copy urges action over Goldstone and MacGowan’s pearl dealings.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate paraphrase of the cable filed on pages 32–33.

subfiles.title: Savage’s request for further seed-oyster information
subfiles.about: Savage forwards growers’ correspondence and asks State for further guidance.
subfiles.summary: He requests the return of Mathias’s papers.

subfiles.title: Headquarters reply on seed-oyster supply
subfiles.from: Harold Fair, for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Headquarters forecasts no 1945 surplus but possible exports in the following season.
subfiles.summary: It estimates 10,000 cases for December 1946–March 1947 and requests a demand estimate.

subfiles.title: Reply to Savage on import arrangements
subfiles.about: State refers the association to the U.S. Commercial Company for future seed-oyster imports.
subfiles.summary: The draft acknowledges the forecast, returns Mathias’s correspondence, and encloses related letters.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram on CID report
subfiles.about: The consulate reports that a detailed CID file on MacGowan and Goldstone is being mailed.
subfiles.summary: The telegram requests a reply on CID access to consular staff and records.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch transmitting CID investigation
subfiles.about: A consular despatch forwards the China Theater investigation.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for the CID material.

subfiles.title: General’s covering letter for investigation
subfiles.about: The general asks that the investigation reach U.S. government recipients.
subfiles.summary: He requests forwarding to State, the Attorney General, the Senate committee, and the Smaller War Plants Corporation.

subfiles.title: Additional consular enclosure
subfiles.about: A badly degraded enclosure accompanies the Shanghai despatch.
subfiles.summary: Its substantive text cannot be reliably recovered from the OCR.

subfiles.title: Reference slip
subfiles.about: An administrative slip notes completion of an action.
subfiles.summary: Reference slip marked “Action completed.”

subfiles.title: Loan of Caraway report
subfiles.about: Burgess lends the MacGowan–Goldstone report under restrictions on copying and disclosure.
subfiles.summary: The report is to be returned.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Caraway report
subfiles.about: Arnold acknowledges receipt of the report.
subfiles.summary: Receipt for one envelope containing Caraway’s report.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser note on report transmission
subfiles.about: Summers explains why the War Department could not transmit the CID report to the Senate committee.
subfiles.summary: Colonel Lincoln said the Department had not been officially apprised of actions taken in China.

subfiles.title: CID investigation of MacGowan and Goldstone
subfiles.from: John F. Stosopf Jr. and George Plotkin, Criminal Investigation Division
subfiles.to: Commanding General, U.S. Forces, China Theater
subfiles.about: CID investigates alleged private pearl trading by men travelling under Senate committee auspices.
subfiles.summary: The report alleges that Goldstone sought to buy or control large quantities of cultured pearls in Shanghai while MacGowan knew of and joined many negotiations. It details financing, purchases, their Japan trip, the seizure of pearls from Goldstone’s military flight, and the cancellation of both men’s air priorities. Investigators question their authority and recommend forwarding the case for further action.

subfiles.title: Reply to Paul Kirimura on pearl-industry survey
subfiles.about: Martin forwards Kirimura’s offer to survey Japan’s cultured-pearl industry.
subfiles.summary: He refers the proposal to an official helping plan personnel for MacArthur’s staff.

subfiles.title: Offer to investigate Japan’s cultured-pearl industry
subfiles.about: Kirimura proposes a one-month survey of Japan’s cultured-pearl industry.
subfiles.summary: He argues that renewed pearl cultivation would provide peaceful employment and cites his industry and Japanese-language experience.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Japanese fishermen and fish stocks
subfiles.about: A Soviet reply addresses Japanese fishing property and fishermen in Soviet-occupied territory.
subfiles.summary: Lozovsky says stocks were destroyed, spoiled, or taken and used; the fishermen’s return remains under consideration.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Manila on travellers’ return
subfiles.about: State requests transport and arrival details for Goldstone and MacGowan.
subfiles.summary: Urgent inquiry about their route to a West Coast port.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: A white telegram copy replaces an unreturned yellow action copy.
subfiles.summary: The notice directs return of the record copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Manila reply on Goldstone and MacGowan
subfiles.about: Manila asks State to clarify its inquiry because the two travellers are unknown there.
subfiles.summary: Brief response to the urgent telegram.

subfiles.title: Tecla inquiry about Japanese cultured pearls
subfiles.about: Tecla asks whether it may buy Japanese-origin pearls already imported through Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Blumenthal asks about State regulations and notes a parallel Treasury inquiry.

subfiles.title: Reply to Tecla on purchase of Japanese pearls
subfiles.about: State gives its view on purchases of Japanese-origin pearls already in U.S. trade.
subfiles.summary: Martin sees no State objection if customs rules are met and there is no direct trade with Japanese nationals. He points to the U.S. Commercial Company for new exports and leaves Trading with the Enemy Act questions to Treasury.

subfiles.title: Memorandum urging transmission of CID report
subfiles.about: Terrill urges prompt forwarding of CID material to the Senate committee and Smaller War Plants Corporation.
subfiles.summary: He describes State as the report’s transmitting agency.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file note
subfiles.about: A short handwritten file note follows the transmission memorandum.
subfiles.summary: The note is largely illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser note on Goldstone’s seized pearls
subfiles.about: The Legal Adviser considers how to answer Goldstone’s request for return of seized pearls.
subfiles.summary: Bishop recommends referring the recovery question to the War Department.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note on Goldstone question
subfiles.about: A colleague forwards the Goldstone question to Summers.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten routing note.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser file sheet
subfiles.about: A nearly blank Legal Adviser sheet bears a reference number.
subfiles.summary: Administrative file sheet.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for attached letter
subfiles.about: A routing slip directs circulation of an attached letter.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten circulation instructions are partly illegible.

subfiles.title: Imperial Pearl Syndicate letter on seized pearls
subfiles.from: Imperial Pearl Syndicate, on behalf of Joseph Goldstone
subfiles.about: The syndicate seeks to preserve Goldstone’s rights and learn how to present his claim for seized pearls.
subfiles.summary: The letter recounts the purchase, customs payments, consular invoice, removal of Goldstone and the pearls from an aircraft, and delays in reaching Washington. It says the War Department was asked to prevent disposal of the pearls. The letter continues beyond page 77.
